meta.title: IFRS 9 Financial Instruments - impairment (5.5 and B5.5): staging, significant increase in credit risk, 12-month and lifetime expected credit losses, forward-looking information, write-off
meta.basis: Prepared 8 October 2026 from the build of specification v4: the staged loan books of July 2024 to August 2026 on the clean install, the Governance Centre's staging and forward-looking settings, the forward-looking chain (fli:correlate), the scenario set of 15.8, and the PHPUnit suite. The PD engine (transition matrices) has not run on the clean install, so the ECL figures there are nil; the rows below audit the mechanics and the settings.
meta.source: IFRS 9 Financial Instruments as issued by the IASB, section 5.5 and B5.5.1 to B5.5.55. The Reserve Bank of Malawi Financial Services (Credit Risk Management for Development Finance Institutions) Directive 2018 (docs/regulatory). Specification: docs/MAIIC_EIR_Engine_Specification_v4_2026-10-07.md sections 3.6, 13, 14, 15, 16.

rows.section_name: A loss allowance for expected credit losses
rows.requirement: Recognise a loss allowance for expected credit losses on a financial asset measured at amortised cost.
rows.engine_comment: TimePhasedEclService computes the allowance per loan as EAD x PD x LGD, discounted at the EIR, for the period; ifrs9:recalculate-ecl runs it per portfolio; the bootstrap runs it for the last period.
rows.compliance_comment: Compliant in mechanics; the PD engine must run for a figure.

rows.section_name: Lifetime ECL on a significant increase in credit risk
rows.requirement: At each reporting date, measure the loss allowance at lifetime ECL if the credit risk has increased significantly since initial recognition.
rows.engine_comment: StagingService stages every period: Stage 2 from 31 days past due in every class (the directive), the SICR flag from the qualitative groups, and the ECL takes the lifetime window for Stage 2.
rows.where_to_see: Governance Centre, Staging & SICR Rules: /stageing-rules; Data Foundation, Loan Book

rows.section_name: 12-month ECL where credit risk has not increased significantly
rows.requirement: Measure the loss allowance at an amount equal to 12-month ECL where the credit risk has not increased significantly since initial recognition.
rows.engine_comment: Stage 1 loans take the 12-month PD window in the ECL service; the staging writes the stage every period.

rows.section_name: Determining a significant increase in credit risk; the 30-days-past-due rebuttable presumption
rows.requirement: Assess the change in the risk of default since initial recognition using reasonable and supportable information; there is a rebuttable presumption that credit risk has increased significantly when payments are more than 30 days past due.
rows.engine_comment: Stage 2 from 31 days past due in every facility class; days counted from the oldest overdue instalment as the directive counts, with the bucket ageing beside it; a rebuttal of the presumption is a governed setting (staging_rebuttal) whose seeded value cites the directive; the LONG_TERM rule proposing 91 days is seeded future-dated and inactive pending CFO sign-off.
rows.general_comment: The O13 rebuttal paper of 8 October.
rows.compliance_comment: Compliant; the presumption is applied, the rebuttal is governed.
rows.where_to_see: Governance Centre, Staging & SICR Rules: /stageing-rules; Data Foundation, Loan Book; Governance Centre: /eir-governance

rows.section_name: Definition of default; the 90-days-past-due rebuttable presumption
rows.requirement: Apply a definition of default consistent with the one used for internal credit risk management; there is a rebuttable presumption that default occurs no later than 90 days past due unless reasonable and supportable information supports a more lagging criterion.
rows.engine_comment: Stage 3 from 91 days for a facility of 12 months or less and for the Mega Farm class, and from 181 days for a medium- or long-term facility, as the RBM directive classifies them; the accounting policy's four-consecutive-missed-instalments trigger lifts a loan to Stage 3 beside the day count. The more lagging criterion rests on the directive, cited on each threshold row.
rows.general_comment: Spec v4 section 3.6 compares the policy (90 days), the November 2025 model (181) and the directive (181/91).
rows.compliance_comment: Compliant; the rebuttal is documented on the threshold rows.
rows.where_to_see: Governance Centre, Staging & SICR Rules: /stageing-rules; Data Foundation, Loan Book

rows.requirement: ECL is an unbiased, probability-weighted amount determined by evaluating a range of possible outcomes, the time value of money, and reasonable and supportable information about past events, current conditions and forecasts of future economic conditions.
rows.engine_comment: Probability weighting across scenarios is built as the governed weighting method (the ECL under each scenario, weighted; sensitivity stored with the set); discounting is at the EIR; the forward-looking chain produces fits from the macro series. The PD engine has not run on the clean install and no fit is approved by a MAIIC reviewer, so the weighted ECL is not yet produced for a period.
rows.compliance_comment: Partially done: the mechanics are in place; the PD run and an approved fit are awaited.
rows.where_to_see: Financial Modelling, ECL Calculation: /expected-credit-loss; Governance Centre, Scenario Sets: /scenario-sets

rows.requirement: The estimate reflects the possibility that a credit loss occurs and the possibility that none occurs; a range of scenarios, at least two, weighted by their probabilities.
rows.engine_comment: The governed scenario set: three or more scenarios, weights summing to 100, the base at least 40 percent and no single weight above 60, every scenario but the base a shock on the base path; the first set (Base 50, Upside 15, Downside 25, Severe 10) is seeded as a proposal for the CFO, each anchored to a year Malawi has lived through.

rows.section_name: Reasonable and supportable information; forward-looking information
rows.requirement: Use information that is reasonably available without undue cost or effort, including forecasts of future economic conditions; where a statistical relationship is used it must be supportable.
rows.engine_comment: Eleven Malawi macro series from the World Bank with their provenance (source, address, fetched-at, who) and a committed snapshot; the forward-looking chain sweeps every driver against every credit-loss proxy over the lag grid under the guardrail (expected sign, R2 cutoff, p-value, minimum observations) and declines a fit that fails with the reason; the structural-events register (the 2023 devaluation, COVID, the policy-rate cycle, the E-Banker take-on) is read by the diagnostics.
rows.general_comment: On the clean install: 209 fits, 39 applied by the guardrail, 170 declined.
rows.compliance_comment: Compliant; an applied fit is a proposal under maker-checker.
rows.where_to_see: Financial Modelling, Forward-Looking Model: /regression; fli:correlate; fli:method-cards; Data Foundation, Macro Statistics

rows.section_name: How forward-looking information reaches the PD
rows.requirement: The method of adjusting the PD for the forecast must be documented and supportable.
rows.engine_comment: Five governed transmission methods, each with a card: what it does, the formula, what it implies, its preconditions checked live against the data with the deciding figure, and a worked example on one loan; a method whose preconditions are not met cannot be selected; the scalar is seeded because the history cannot yet support the richer methods.
rows.where_to_see: Financial Modelling, Forward-Looking Model: /regression; fli:correlate; fli:method-cards; Governance Centre, the cards inline on the setting: /eir-governance; fli:method-cards

rows.requirement: Where information is not available at the instrument level, assess on a collective basis grouped by shared credit-risk characteristics.
rows.engine_comment: Credit-loss proxies are produced for the book and per product group (NPL ratio, Stage 3 share, 12-month default rate), and the segment-specific scalar is a governed method; the PD transition matrices by grade run from their screen and are not yet in the bootstrap chain.
rows.where_to_see: Financial Modelling, Forward-Looking Model: /regression; fli:correlate; fli:method-cards; Financial Modelling, PD Model

rows.requirement: The cash shortfalls reflect the cash flows expected from collateral and other credit enhancements that are part of the contractual terms.
rows.engine_comment: LGD runs from the LGD screens (monthly and cumulative); the security register (P2_11, 185 rows) is landed and 31 active accounts carry no security on it (the request to Credit of 7 October).
rows.compliance_comment: Evidence needed: the collateral for the 31 accounts; the valuations.
rows.where_to_see: Financial Modelling, LGD Model; Data Foundation, Collateral Register

rows.requirement: Discount the expected credit losses at the EIR determined at initial recognition.
rows.engine_comment: EclDiscountRateService takes the locked EIR of the loan (the contractual rate where none is locked, and says so on the row); the bootstrap solves and locks the EIR before the ECL for this reason.

rows.requirement: Write off the gross carrying amount when there is no reasonable expectation of recovery.
rows.engine_comment: No write-off has been posted in E-Banker since the take-on (DD_16i returned no rows); the policy is MAIIC's to state.

rows.section_name: The Mega Farm loans in the allowance
rows.requirement: Loans extended under the Government's Mega Farm programme (losses to the fund; MAIIC's 5 percent share) must be in the ECL on a documented basis.
rows.engine_comment: The system holds a November 2025 Mega Farm loan book of 3,490 loans across six GLs (K54.85 bn), found by the build, staged under the MEGA_FARM class (91 days); the programme's treatment (decision D30: out of the EIR engine, in the ECL module, 5 percent share on net) and the PD method (seeded: the agricultural-sector PD scaled to the programme) are governed settings awaiting the CFO's confirmation.
rows.general_comment: Spec v4 section 16; the O22 paper of 8 October.
rows.compliance_comment: Evidence needed: the CFO's confirmation of D30; how the K39.76 bn provision of 2025 was arrived at; the monthly Mega Farm books.
rows.where_to_see: Financial Modelling, Mega Farm Programme: /megafarm; Governance Centre: /eir-governance

findings.finding: The PD and LGD of the clean install are the bootstrap's, not MAIIC's
findings.what_was_found: PdEngineService and LgdEngineService run the transition matrix and the cohort workout under the bootstrap label; no MAIIC reviewer has key-locked a matrix or an LGD calculation in the system.
findings.impact: The ECL of 8.33bn at August 2026 is a system figure awaiting review.
findings.recommended_action: A reviewer key-locks the matrix and the LGD on their screens; the ECL is then re-run under the approved scenario set.

findings.finding: No fit is approved by a MAIIC reviewer
findings.what_was_found: The chain applied 39 fits by the guardrail; approval of a fit for use in the FLI route is a maker-checker decision not yet taken.
findings.impact: The forward-looking adjustment is the manual overlay at zero until then.
findings.recommended_action: A reviewer approves a fit on the FLI Adjustments screen; a second person reviews.

findings.finding: The Mega Farm provision basis is undocumented in the system
findings.what_was_found: The 2025 statements carry K39.76 bn against K48.7 bn Stage 3; the November 2025 book in the system is mostly Stage 1 by days past due.
findings.impact: The ECL golden number at 31 December 2025 cannot be set.
findings.recommended_action: The CFO confirms D30 and the provisioning method; the monthly Mega Farm books are loaded by the feed (MF_01 to MF_08).
